The formal problem is defined within the following assumptions and operationalizations. Note that Assumptions A2 and A4 currently lack precise mathematical definitions and require human input:
- A1: Spherically symmetric collapse of massive stars with isotropic pressure.
- A2: Matter fields satisfy the Averaged Null Energy Condition (AANEC) along complete null generators. [Needs Human Input]
- A3: Spacetime is globally hyperbolic and sufficiently regular for trapped-surface arguments.
- A4: An explicit averaged null-convergence/focusing condition holds along the relevant generators. [Needs Human Input]
- A5: Non-black-hole remnants are modeled as stable equilibrium objects obeying a bounded compactness limit.

Based on these assumptions, the primary hypothesis posits that if spherically symmetric stellar collapse satisfies AANEC, global hyperbolicity, regular matter fields, complete null generators, and an explicit averaged null-convergence/focusing condition, then reaching a model-dependent compactness threshold forces trapped-surface formation. Consequently, a secondary proposition suggests that stable non-black-hole remnants above a compactness-dependent mass scale are excluded within this restricted model class.
